title: 1. Start here: the daily operating cycle
paras: My Project Management v45 | User manual, process flow and dashboard/report data guide | 23 November 2026 | Qatar time.

The application follows Customer > Project > Companies > Modules > Activities > Daily allocations > Actual hours > Timesheets and reports. The daily activity entry uses one Activity Date and Hours. One man-day is 8 hours; a half-day session equivalent is 4 hours. Enter net decimal hours: 1.5 means 1 hour 30 minutes, not 1 hour 50 minutes.

For a first setup, the workspace owner completes masters, users and permissions before the project manager creates projects. Each morning, the manager reviews pending work and allocates the day. Each consultant reports actual hours and remarks. The manager reviews client deductions, follow-ups and reports.

This manual describes the IIS / SQL Server edition. Hosted preview or browser-local demo data is separate from your live company database. Sign in at the company IIS address to work on shared company records.

Project manager / lead with rights
Review company modules, consultants, baseline activities, effort budget and go-live dates. Configure AMC contract where applicable.
4. Plan and allocate
Project manager / permitted lead
Create daily hours-only allocations or prepare weekly visits. A weekly worksheet creates daily allocations; it is not a second actual-entry register.

Allocator
Review the individual WhatsApp message or full-team daily report and send it in WhatsApp. Sharing is user initiated.

Open Update actual, review Activity Date and hours, enter remarks, status and client deduction Yes/No where needed; save.
7. Decide next action
Employee and project manager
Completed: review company/go-live readiness. More sessions, waiting or open: record a clear note; allocate a later visit when the client confirms.
8. Review delivery
Project manager
Check timesheets, client-hour budget, pending work, AMC visits/hours and project risks. Correct entries only with the proper role rights.
9. Report and close
Project manager
Generate date-range project/PSR reports, review notes and export. Confirm each company/module go-live separately; completing tasks alone does not mark all companies Live.

title: 3. Roles, login and permissions
paras: Use your company email/password login. A team profile and a sign-in account are related but different: adding a name to Team management does not itself prove that a usable login has been created. Use User master / SQL Server & accounts as available to the workspace owner to create or manage company accounts.

Workspace owners control role configuration. Role master defines roles such as Project manager, Project lead and Consultant; Role permissions defines their allowed actions. Custom roles can inherit a base role. The actual permission matrix is authoritative; a job title or being named Project Manager does not grant every permission automatically.

Project assignment gives scope/visibility. Project manager, in-charge, module membership and task participation can give project access, but task and actual-entry visibility still follow the account permissions. An employee with partial access can see incomplete project totals. Use an authorized account with full project visibility for a complete client report.

Role name/code, base role, active status and allowed actions
Controls visibility, edits, corrections, scheduling and exports.

Allocations use employee IDs. Maintain numbers in the expected international format before WhatsApp sharing.

Code, module name, description, active status
Select modules by checkbox in projects and configure module people/company plans. Deactivate instead of deleting history.

New Implementation / AMC / Warranty / Office, or active configured types
Project stage/type selects the activity list for new allocations. Existing work retains its recorded type when the project stage changes.

Only active matching-type activities are offered for new work. Codes are unique; names are unique within a type. Activity type is fixed after creation.

title: 5. Create and expand a project
paras: Open Projects > create a new project. Choose the customer and stage/type; enter the project code, name, contact, industry, Project Manager and Project In-charge. Review start and target go-live dates. New-entry date fields default to today and are editable.

Select module checkboxes. Each selected module needs a primary in-charge; tick additional people where several consultants will work on it. Project-level module assignments are defaults, not automatic daily tasks.

Enter Number of companies (normally 1 to 100) and real company names. Saving creates company records with the selected module defaults. Company names must be unique within the project. Review each company card afterwards.

To expand later, open the project and choose Edit project / modules / company count. Increase the company count and/or check additional modules at any project stage. Existing modules remain selected. Count cannot be reduced below existing company records, to protect their plans and history.

The default option adds newly selected modules to existing companies without replacing consultant overrides. A live company receiving a new module becomes Not ready for the additional scope; existing actual go-live dates and module history are retained. New companies inherit current project defaults. The separate matching-default option is opt-in for owner changes.

Changing project defaults does not reallocate existing daily work. Edit the allocation itself when a different employee must perform a task. Company-specific names, consultants and go-live fields are maintained through Edit / go-live on the company card.

title: 6. Plan companies, activities and budgets
paras: Within a project, review each company and its modules. Use Add activity to build a dated baseline, or apply an implementation template and then review every generated activity, consultant and date. Baseline start/finish dates remain useful in Project plan even though Daily Allocation uses one activity date.

An activity has one primary task owner and may contain multiple daily allocations to different employees. Do not confuse task ownership with the person on each allocation. Baseline effort is stored in half-day session equivalents: planned hours / 4 for new hours-only tasks.

Use the project client implementation budget to enter contracted man-days and classify any legacy session hours. Budget hours = contracted man-days x 8. A project with no budget shows Not set; setting a budget does not create or approve work.

Keep company/module go-live status and actual dates under review. A project is treated as completed only when it has activities, task-count progress is 100%, and all configured companies are marked Live. A report does not itself change go-live status.

title: 7. Allocate daily work: one date and hours
paras: Open Daily allocations and choose Create task & allocate. Select project, company, module and activity. The type comes from the project for new work. Optionally select a matching existing planned activity instead of creating another task.

Enter Activity Date and Planned Hours. Choose onsite/offsite, client/internal and one or more employees. Add clear instructions and save. Each employee receives an allocation. For a shared session, planned hours apply to each selected employee.

Hours must be above 0 and at most 24 per allocation. Enter net hours excluding breaks. No start/end clock time is required. A new task derives its baseline start/finish from this one activity date; existing task baselines are preserved.

To change pending work, use Edit allocation. Rescheduling rights are required to change date or planned hours. Once work is reported, retain the original allocation date and add another allocation for a later visit. Editing an allocation does not move another employee allocation automatically.

Daily cards and the work table use allocation date, which may differ from actual work date. A changed actual work date will therefore appear in a different timesheet period without moving the original planned allocation.

title: 8. Weekly visits, calendar and WhatsApp
paras: Use Weekly visit worksheet to select employee, customer, project, matching activity, optional planned task, date, times, onsite/offsite and notes. The weekly worksheet retains clock scheduling; the simplified daily form does not require it. Saving the worksheet creates the canonical daily allocations.

New weekly rows default to today when today is in the selected week; choosing another week uses that week. Review the selected week before saving. Daily allocations are the place to complete remaining instructions and actual reporting.

Hours-only daily allocations appear as date-based calendar entries and export as all-day ICS events with the hours in the title. They do not reserve a clock-time slot. Existing timed visits and meetings keep their original scheduled times. Use the calendar and weekly plan to review dates; use Daily allocations to edit allocation records.

Use the WhatsApp action on an individual allocation to prepare a message and employee link. Review and send it yourself in WhatsApp. The team report can be downloaded/copied and attached to a group. The application does not silently send WhatsApp messages.

The link must use an IIS address reachable by the consultant. localhost works only on the computer hosting IIS. Sharing a link does not create an account or grant access. The employee must use their company login and have the correct role/project access.

title: 9. Report actual activity
paras: Open Daily allocations, Team/My dashboard, or a timesheet row and choose Update actual. The simplified form has Activity Date, Actual Hours, Status, Completion %, Outcome/remarks and client-deduction choice. An AMC onsite activity may also show a visit checkbox.

When no actual report exists, planned hours are loaded for review. Saved actual hours and date take priority when reopening. Opening or cancelling the form never records hours. Review the date/hours, enter what was actually delivered and save.

Enter 0 for a status-only update. Completed work requires positive actual hours and an outcome. Future actual work is blocked. More sessions, awaiting confirmation and open updates require a clear follow-up note. Use another daily allocation to schedule the next confirmed visit.

For a team session, each employee must choose whether their own client-tagged hours deduct from the client. Internal work never deducts from the client. All positive employee hours still appear in timesheets, regardless of deduction. An authorized manager can correct actuals or deductions; audit history records the updater.

Task-level actual start/finish dates are derived from recorded work dates. If one employee completes a shared activity while other allocations remain incomplete, the activity can remain In progress. Allocation status and overall activity status are intentionally distinct.

Old clock/session entries remain readable. Direct numeric hours take priority when an entry is saved in the new form; an explicit numeric zero overrides old clock values. Existing timing fields are not used to invent another visit or duplicate actual hours.

title: 11. Worked example: two consultants, one session
paras: Finance training is allocated to Aisha and Daniel for 4 hours each. They both report 3 actual hours. Aisha selects Yes for client deduction; Daniel selects No. Both entries are Client-tagged.

Timesheets show Aisha 3 + Daniel 3 = 6 employee hours. Client deduction is 3 hours, not 6. Client non-deducted hours are 3. An 80-hour client budget has 77 hours remaining. Client man-days consumed are 3 / 8 = 0.375 (displayed with report rounding).

If the same shared onsite visit qualifies for an AMC contract and both required people attend, visit hours are counted once using the maximum attendee hours: 3 hours, not 6. If the contract requires 4 hours per visit, this visit is short even though employee timesheets total 6 hours.
Planned hours, employee actual hours, client deduction and AMC visit hours answer different questions. Do not expect them to be equal.

title: 12. Where application data is stored and loaded from
paras: In the live SQL edition, records are stored in the configured MyProjectManagement SQL Server database. The browser loads an authorized workspace snapshot through the application API, then renders dashboards and reports from those records. Refreshes are checked periodically (normally around 10 seconds in this build). A failed save is not evidence that SQL stored the change.

SQL reporting views read the same canonical JSON records; they are not separate manually maintained ledgers. In the browser preview/local mode, data lives in browser storage instead, so clearing/changing browsers can affect demo records. Use the live SQL edition for shared team data.

paras: Use the application for ordinary editing. Direct SQL changes can bypass validation, relationships, audit and permissions; an administrator should take a backup and understand the JSON model before any repair. Never share SQL credentials with consultants.

Older entries fall back to stored clock times/breaks, then legacy half-day units. SQL views preserve those rules. v45 adds documentation and does not require another schema change.

title: 16. AMC process and alerts
paras: For an AMC-stage project enter contract start/end, cycle (daily, alternate days, weekly, monthly, quarterly, six-monthly or yearly), visits per cycle, hours per visit and required staff. Review the suggested weekly visits before creating allocations.

Only onsite allocation evidence within the contract/cycle is used for compliance. A shared session is grouped by its AMC visit link or team group; independent hours-only allocations use their own visit keys. Per-visit credited hours use the maximum attendee hours, not the sum of employee timesheets.

Qualification requires the required people and sufficient per-visit hours. A short visit can contribute attended hours while still failing the qualifying-visit target. Closed-cycle visit/hour gaps create overdue alerts; future cycles should be reviewed for missing scheduling.

Employee timesheets and client deductions remain separate. Marking No for client deduction does not remove the employee hours, and does not automatically invalidate a legitimate onsite AMC visit. Offsite/internal support may still be employee work without being an onsite compliance visit.

title: 17. Daily checks and troubleshooting
rows: Allocation is missing
Selected allocation date, project/company/module, employee/status filters and role/project scope. Confirm that save succeeded in the live shared workspace.
Timesheet is missing
Positive saved actual hours, actual work date, employee filter and access rights. Opening Update actual or allocating planned hours does not create a timesheet.
Client total differs from employee total
Client/Internal tag, each person deduction Yes/No, legacy classification and cumulative versus period scope. Team hours are not automatically a client charge.
Progress percentages differ
Project percentage counts completed tasks; plan/company progress weights task completion by planned effort. Neither equals budget consumption.
Task remains In progress after completion
Other daily allocations may remain incomplete. Check each person allocation and separate company/module go-live.
AMC visit is missing or short
Contract/cycle dates, onsite mode, visit mark, group/visit key, required attendees and hours per visit.
Report is incomplete
Use the correct date basis and a fully authorized account. SQL workspace/project parameters and browser filters must refer to the same project. A partial-access login sees partial data.
Cannot save / another save pending
Read the displayed error, wait for current shared save or resolve the conflict, confirm the current version, then retry. Avoid opening parallel edits in several tabs.
401 or login problem
Company email/login status, credentials, session and IIS address. A database permission repair does not fix invalid sign-in credentials.
App works but SQL reports show wrong numeric hours
Confirm the v31 HoursOnly reporting patch was applied to the same database used by IIS.
WhatsApp link cannot open
Use a reachable company IIS URL, not localhost or a local file path. Confirm the employee company account and permissions.
Data differs in another browser
Check live SQL sign-in versus demo/browser storage and the selected workspace. Browser demo data is not the SQL database.

title: 18. Administration, backups and release control
paras: Keep the application version, database patch history and a backup together. Verify the displayed version after an IIS update. Back up both SQL data and the deployed site before upgrading; retain appsettings configuration, web.config and the authentication key directory.

For v45, install the updated application and guide. There is no additional SQL schema change over v35. If upgrading from an earlier version, use the cumulative v45 upgrade to include the v31 numeric-hours reporting and v35 change-request prerequisites.

Preserve the existing IIS configuration and keys when replacing publish contents. Restart the application pool and hard-refresh the browser. Do not run a fresh-database setup script as a routine update. Complete rollback uses the paired application/database backup; old application versions may not understand direct-hour entries.

The full manual and process-flow PDFs/Word files in this release contain examples and operating instructions only, with no live company records or credentials. Users can open User manual & process flow in the application; the online and PDF/Word versions contain the same guide content.

title: 20. Choose an enterprise theme
paras: Open Appearance & Help > Appearance, or use the theme button in the top bar. Choose Midnight Blue, Light Workspace or Charcoal & Amber. The default is Midnight Blue. Each theme applies to navigation, dashboard panels, tables, forms and dialogs.

Midnight Blue uses a navy navigation rail and blue actions. Light Workspace uses a white sidebar and indigo controls. Charcoal & Amber uses a charcoal sidebar and amber actions. All three retain light data surfaces for readable forms and reports.

Choose Comfortable or Compact table spacing. Theme and spacing are saved only in this browser preferences. They do not change shared company data, employee permissions, saved actuals or report calculations. Another device can use another theme. Clearing browser storage resets the preference.

PDF/Word manuals and printed PSR reports keep their own document design. v45 also introduces a consolidated dashboard KPI ribbon, a project-register layout, sharper table and input borders, and local system fonts. No Google font download is required for the application theme.

title: 21. Change requests: technical feasibility and revisions
paras: Open Projects & Planning > Change requests. The workflow is Initiator draft > Project Manager feasibility review > CTO review > Technically feasible and ready to share with the client. Consultants, project leads and team leads can initiate requests when their configured role permits and they have project access.

Before first use the administrator runs the REQUIRED v35 SQL migration. It adds ChangeRequests and ChangeRequestDocuments tables and seeds missing CR permissions plus CTO and Team lead role templates. Create the actual CTO employee profile and company login, assign role rights, and confirm Project Manager in each project. The initiator, assigned PM and CTO must be different active people.

Create a draft with project, CTO approver, title, expected change, revision reason and numbered change points. PM comes from Project Master. Each non-empty line becomes P1, P2, etc. Save the draft, then upload its Word file and submit. A Word document is required for every submitted revision.

Word uploads support .docx and .doc up to 5 MB each. Uploads are retained, with the latest document designated for submission. Submitted documents cannot be replaced. The app gives a read-only .docx text preview with D1, D2 paragraph references; formatting, images and Word tracked changes are not reproduced. Legacy .doc files must be downloaded and opened in Word. Use original-file download for complete formatting. Text previews show at most 2000 non-empty paragraphs, with up to 5000 characters in each paragraph.

The assigned PM reviews the exact revision and chooses Approve, Amendment, Clarification or Meeting. Comments can refer to numbered points or D paragraph references. Amendment/clarification/meeting needs an explanation. A meeting request records a proposed date; confirm and create the actual appointment through Meetings. It does not silently book a calendar slot.

PM approval sends the revision to its assigned CTO. CTO has the same decision choices. CTO cannot approve before PM. Both approvals are required for Technically feasible. Use Awaiting my review to find your inbox; the register checks for updates around every 15 seconds while open, but does not replace a form while it is being edited.

Returned/meeting-requested revisions are read only. The initiator creates a new revision, explains the amendment, edits the points, uploads the revised Word file and submits again to PM. Client feedback after technical approval follows the same new-revision process. Approval is never copied to a new revision.

Technically feasible means this exact revision is ready to share, not that the client or commercial terms are approved. Download that approved revision Word file and send it through your normal process. The app does not send email or WhatsApp automatically, and its private document URLs are not public client links.

Revision history retains points, documents, reviewer decisions, point/paragraph comments, proposed meetings and audit timestamps. The register shows up to the latest 200 accessible requests. Filters show My requests, Awaiting my review or Ready for client. Company login, active role permissions and assignment are enforced by the server.

title: 22. Change-request data, access and backup
paras: CR records use dedicated SQL tables and authenticated /api/change-requests endpoints, separate from the ordinary workspace snapshot. The CR register counts current revision states. My requests uses initiator ID. Awaiting my review uses current Pending PM/CTO status plus assigned reviewer ID. Ready for client uses current Technically feasible state. Historical approved revisions remain available even if the latest revision is being amended.

Role permissions include Create/revise own change requests, Review as Project Manager, Approve as CTO and View all CRs within project scope. Initiators and assigned reviewers can read their request and revision history. Broad register visibility does not itself give authority to approve. Only the assigned reviewer at the current pending stage can decide.

Word bytes are stored in dbo.ChangeRequestDocuments.Content with file name, revision and SHA-256 hash. They are not written under wwwroot or a public upload folder. Every download/preview checks the active company login, workspace and CR access. CR metadata and files use no-store responses. Changes use a version check; a stale update returns a conflict instead of overwriting another decision.

Full SQL database backups include CR metadata, approval history and Word documents. The ordinary workspace JSON export/import does NOT include these dedicated CR tables or document bytes. Keep SQL backups and allow for attachment storage growth. There is no CR delete function in this version. If a project is removed, retain CR audit history; creating further revisions requires a valid project record.

First installation requires Database-ChangeRequests-v35.sql, or the cumulative v45 upgrade. Existing v31 numeric-hours reporting remains required. A fresh workspace created after installation receives CTO/Team lead templates from owner initialization. The Word text preview is an app review aid, not an embedded Word editor.

dbo.vwChangeRequestApprovals
Review decisions, reviewer/time, general/point/paragraph comments and proposed meeting date.

title: 23. Upload Activity Master and Project Plan from Excel
paras: Activity Master: Masters & Setup > Activity master > Download Excel template / Upload Excel. Project Plan: Projects & Planning > Project plan > Download Excel template / Upload Excel. Import buttons follow existing master/plan permissions. In the company IIS edition they save to SQL Server; in the browser demo they save only to that browser.

Download the template from the appropriate screen. Fill the first worksheet below its heading row. In-app templates include reference sheets for available activity types or projects/companies/modules, activity codes and consultant IDs/names. Those reference sheets are not imported. Standalone blank templates are included in this release; in-app templates are better for matching your company records.

Activity Master columns: Activity Code, Activity Name, Activity Type, Description, Status. Code/name allow up to 140 characters; type must match an existing active type code or name. Status is Active or Inactive (default Active). Description is optional, maximum 1000 characters. Codes are unique across the catalog and names are unique within their type, including inactive records.

Project Plan columns: Plan Reference, Project Code, Company, Module, Activity Code, Consultant, Planned Start, Planned Finish, Planned Hours, Priority, Notes. Use an existing accessible project and exact company name. Company may be blank only when the project has one company. Module must be active and selected for that company; General is allowed. Activity code must be active and match the project stage. Consultant accepts exact ID, unique name or company email; using IDs avoids duplicate-name ambiguity.

Plan Reference is your unique import line code (up to 50 characters), unique within a project. Re-uploading the same references is rejected. Identical company/module/activity/consultant/date baselines are also rejected, even with another reference. Import is ADD ONLY: it never overwrites existing activities or actual work.

Plan dates accept yyyy-mm-dd text or normal Excel date values. Empty date cells default to today and show a preview note; date headers are still required. Finish must not be before start. Planned Hours are total baseline effort, above 0 and at most 4000. They become half-day session equivalents by dividing by 4. Priority is Low, Medium or High (default Medium). Notes are optional, up to 2000 characters.

Select Upload Excel, choose .xlsx or comma-separated UTF-8 CSV, then Preview file. The first sheet/header row 1 is used; maximum file size is 5 MB and maximum 500 data rows. Formulas, protected/encrypted formats and .xls/.xlsm are not supported: paste values and save as .xlsx. Keep codes/references as text to retain leading zeros. For old browsers unable to decompress .xlsx, use a current Chrome/Edge or save the first worksheet as CSV.

Preview shows normalized values, source row numbers, errors and warnings. No records are saved at preview. Import all rows is enabled only when every row is valid. Correct the original Excel file and preview again if errors appear. There is no partial-row import. A shared workspace version check rejects stale previews: reload/re-preview instead of overwriting another user changes.

Project Plan upload creates To do baseline tasks with dates, owner and effort. It does NOT create daily allocations, employee actuals, timesheets or go-live events. Schedule imported work from Daily allocations or the weekly worksheet. Uploaded activity master rows become selectable by type in later plans/allocations.

Activity import uses Manage Activity Master plus View All Projects permissions. Plan import uses Manage Plans within each project scope. Shared preview/commit runs server-side validation again before one database transaction. The file itself is read in the browser; row data is sent only to the company API and the source Excel file is not stored as an attachment. No new SQL tables/schema are required by v45. Existing v31/v35 prerequisites still apply.
rows: Activity Master
Workspaces.SettingsJson.activityMaster, through the existing catalog validation. Existing codes and same-type names are rejected; catalog limit remains 500 total activities.
Project Plan
WorkspaceRecords task JSON. planImportReference, planImportedBy and planImportedAt identify imported baselines. Existing record relationships and report formulas remain unchanged.
Batch failure / concurrent change
No rows from a rejected SQL transaction are saved. Fix the sheet or preview again against the latest workspace revision.

title: 24. Upload the Weekly Site Visits plan from Excel
paras: Open Projects & Planning > Weekly site visits and select Week containing. Then choose Download Excel template / Upload Excel. The import is bound to that Monday-to-Sunday week; every visit date must fall inside it. The selected week is displayed in the upload dialog.

Fill the first worksheet, one row per consultant. Columns: Visit Reference, Activity Date, Project Code, Company, Module, Activity Code, Consultant, Start Time, End Time, Work Mode, Hours Classification, Notes, Existing Task ID. In-app templates include project/company/module/customer references, activity codes, consultant IDs and open task IDs. Standalone templates are blank and generic.

Visit Reference is a new unique visit code within the project (maximum 50 characters). Repeat it only for different people attending the SAME company/module/activity/date/start/end/mode/classification/existing task. This creates one shared task/session with separate employee allocations. A different session needs another reference. Already-imported references are blocked, even if the file changes employee or date.

Activity Date accepts yyyy-mm-dd text or real Excel dates. Empty dates default to today in the preview, and must still be within the selected week. Start Time/End Time accept 24-hour HH:mm or real Excel time fractions. The end must be later on the same day; overnight visits are not supported. Planned hours are end minus start, with zero break. Daily actuals are entered later as net hours.

Project, company, active module and activity code must already exist. Activity type must match the current project stage. Consultant accepts exact ID, unique name or company email. Customer is inherited from the project. Work Mode is Onsite/Offsite (default Onsite); Hours Classification is Client/Internal (default Client). Notes allow 2000 characters.

Existing Task ID is optional. It must be an open task matching this project/company/module/activity/type, and the consultant must be its primary owner or an existing allocation participant. Leave it blank to create a new planned activity. Existing baseline dates, effort, import reference and actual history are preserved when linking a task.

Preview checks access, row references, the selected week, duplicate consultants and time conflicts within the file, existing timed daily allocations and scheduled meetings. Date-based hours-only allocations do not reserve a clock slot, so they are not treated as time overlaps. Fix every error before Import all rows. There is no partial import or overwrite of old visits.

Import creates canonical daily allocations with weekly-plan links. Those same rows appear in Weekly Site Visits, Daily Allocations and the application calendar. They start Planned with zero actual work, so no actual timesheet is created until the employee or authorized manager reports actual hours.

Shared sessions retain a common team group so later actual updates ask each attendee about client-hour deduction. All employee time remains in timesheets regardless of deduction. AMC compliance still uses onsite evidence, attendance, cycle dates and visit hours; importing a visit does not itself confirm it was delivered.

Use Edit daily details for later schedule changes with the proper rights. If a timed row is changed into an hours-only daily allocation, the weekly screen/export shows hours without a booked clock slot, matching its date-based calendar entry. A reported allocation date remains protected.

The upload accepts .xlsx or UTF-8 CSV, up to 500 rows / 5 MB; formulas and .xls/.xlsm are unsupported. Preview is read-only; commit revalidates against the current shared workspace revision. The live IIS edition saves to SQL; the browser demo saves locally. Rights required: Manage Weekly Plans plus Assign Tasks within project scope; Manage Plans is not additionally required.
rows: Weekly links
Task allocation JSON: weeklyPlanId, weeklyWeek, weeklyImportReference, weeklyImportedBy and weeklyImportedAt.
Shared visit
One task/session per project/reference group unless linking an existing task; multiple people receive separate allocations with a common teamGroupId.
Daily/calendar/report data
The same allocation date/time/mode and planned hours feed weekly and daily screens, generated calendar events and planned work reports. Actuals and timesheets are not pre-created.
Database installation
No new SQL tables or schema change in v45. Existing v31 reporting and v35 Change Request prerequisites still apply.

title: 25. Correct an upload in the preview
paras: Activity Master, Project Plan and Weekly Site Visits previews are editable. Your original uploaded values remain visible, even when they do not match a system master.

Choose existing active reference values from dropdowns. Project selection filters companies and activities; company selection filters modules. Consultants show ID/name/email. Other cells support direct text correction.

Any edit immediately blocks import. Click Revalidate rows to check the edited batch against current data and permissions. Correct every error, then Import all rows. The workbook is not reread during revalidation.
Use Previous rows and Next rows for batches over 25 rows; all edits are retained across pages. Dates use yyyy-mm-dd, visit times HH:mm, hours decimal.

Changing project or company retains other entered values for your review. Old mismatches remain explicitly visible until replaced. Selecting a new file or closing the form discards unsaved corrections.

Corrections change the import rows only; they do not rename or add system master records. Uploads remain add-only and atomic, subject to the same authorization, revision and duplicate/conflict checks. No database migration is required for v45.

title: 26. Import progress, validation and save results
paras: Import all rows rechecks the current rows before saving. The footer beside the buttons displays checking, saving and server-waiting progress so messages remain visible on a long preview.

If rows become invalid, no rows are saved. A summary lists the original Excel row numbers and reasons across all pages. Click a row button to jump to its editable cells, correct them, then revalidate.

A missing preview, changed cells, revoked permissions or pending shared changes display an explicit reason instead of silently returning. Shared revision changes stop the attempt for review and revalidation.

Server errors remain visible in the footer and the form stays open with your corrections. Import success shows the saved row count. If saving is confirmed but refresh fails, reload the workspace and do not import those rows again.

Do not resubmit while the footer says the server is still responding. The form prevents repeated submissions and closing during a save. If the response is uncertain, reload and revalidate before retrying; already-saved rows will be flagged as duplicates.

title: 27. Open and save each project plan separately
paras: Open Projects & Planning > Project plan. First select a project from the accessible project list. Its code, stage, current project status and visible activity progress identify the project you are opening.

The opened workspace shows only that project plan, current activity status, progress and planned versus actual effort. Company, module, person, status and date filters refine that project. Reset filters keeps the project selected.
Use the project dropdown or Choose another project to switch. Opening a project or company plan from Project Master goes directly to the corresponding project and company.

Plan activity and Edit plan retain a fixed project. Saving updates only that project task. Plan export uses the selected project and current filters. Project status is read from Project Master; activity progress uses saved task and actual updates.

Open the target project before Excel upload. The modal freezes its ID; blank Project Code cells inherit its code, while another project code is a row error. Template project reference sheets and preview choices are scoped to the opened project. Both server preview and commit validate scope.

Existing records already carry project references and are retained. No SQL migration or data conversion is needed. Performance and other reporting screens retain their existing workspace-wide options and permission checks.

title: 28. AMC Plan vs Actual: contract delivery
paras: AMC projects do not use implementation baseline progress. Set the project stage to AMC and configure contract dates, site-visit cycle, required visits, hours per visit and required attendees.

Opening the project plan or project details shows AMC Plan vs Actual. Plan values come from the contract requirements. Scheduled and actual values come from that project onsite AMC daily allocations and actual updates, using the existing AMC compliance calculation.

Each cycle shows required visits/hours, scheduled qualifying visits/hours, actual attended and qualifying visits, credited onsite hours, remaining requirements and status. Cycles extend through today or the review week, whichever is later. Short closed cycles are overdue; current short cycles remain open.

A shared onsite visit counts once using the longest attendee actual hours; a qualifying visit also needs the required duration and all required attendees. Offsite support, employee timesheet totals and client deductions stay separate.

Use Weekly site visits or Daily allocations to schedule AMC work and submit actuals. Implementation baseline activity creation and plan Excel upload are not shown in the AMC workspace. Existing records remain stored.

Export AMC Plan vs Actual includes only this project contract cycles. View AMC compliance permission is required. Unconfigured contracts show a setup prompt. Implementation project plans retain their existing workflow.

title: 29. Office: allocate directly and update actuals
paras: Office projects have no project baseline plan or plan-versus-actual comparison. Set the project stage to Office, then use Daily allocations to create the activity and allocate people/date/hours.

Allocated people submit actual date/hours, completion status and remarks through Update actual. Project managers can update others according to role permissions. Existing actual-entry and billing rights remain in force.

Office entries in the plan project chooser open Daily allocations directly. Office project details show a date-based direct work register with allocation and actual-update actions. Allocation entry opened there keeps the Office project fixed.

Baseline activity creation, project plan templates, baseline comparison and plan export are not offered for Office. Project Plan Excel imports reject Office rows in server preview and commit; Office is omitted from plan template reference sheets.

Office hours remain included in employee timesheets and existing daily/hour reports. Existing client/internal classifications and client-deduction choices are preserved. Historical Office records are not deleted.
AMC projects continue to use contract Plan vs Actual. Implementation projects retain their project plan workflow. No database migration is needed over v41.

title: 30. Install and use the mobile companion
paras: Open the company HTTPS address ending /mobile.html. iPhone: Safari > Share > Add to Home Screen. Android: Chrome menu > Install app / Add to Home screen. This is a PWA, not a native app-store APK/IPA. The company server must be reachable from the phone over its network/VPN with a trusted certificate.

Sign in using the same company email/password. Today shows allocations, pending work and actual-hour summaries. Work offers daily allocation, actual updates and quick entry. Visits shows the weekly schedule. Hours provides date-range timesheets and actual-entry actions. More includes meetings, project status, installation help, password and sign-out.

Mobile and desktop share the same authenticated server, project/role checks and database records. Actual updates feed employee timesheets; they do not create duplicate copied timesheets. Implementation, AMC and Office status retain their separate workflows.

Online access is required to load/save work. Offline submissions are blocked. Only public offline help/icons are cached; API/login/workspace data are not cached by the service worker. Watch shared Saving/saved/error status and use backup/reload recovery for failed saves.

Use a real company hostname, not localhost. No SQL credentials belong on the phone. Home-screen installation does not require Apple/Google developer signing, but physical-device acceptance testing is required after deployment.

title: 31. Instant work, team allocation and pending sign-offs
paras: For unexpected work, choose Quick work - for me in desktop Daily allocations or mobile Today/Work/Hours. Select project, activity, date, hours and notes. Allocated saves a task/daily allocation to yourself; Completed also saves actual hours into your timesheet.

The self-work permission is separate from general team assignment. Existing project access and an active staff profile are required. The owner can disable Create instant work allocated to self in Role permissions. Owners without a staff-linked login should use a staff company account for personal work.
Managers use Create task & allocate for employees. Both desktop and mobile pending lists retain uncompleted allocations across dates, including project/CR sign-off follow-ups.

Allocate follow-up / sign-off task records a task subject, assignee, activity, due date and instructions. Completion-only tasks require a dated completion remark and create no timesheet hours. Hourly tasks use ordinary actual-hours updates.
Formal CR approvals/signatures remain separate; completing a tracking follow-up is not an approval. Existing formal approval roles and document workflow remain unchanged.

title: 32. Import Customer Master and Project Master from Excel
paras: First use Masters & Setup > Customer master > Download Excel template / Upload Excel. Then use Projects & Planning > Projects for Project Master upload. These imports add records only; existing codes are never overwritten.

Customer template fields are Customer Code (50), Customer Name (160), Status (Active/Inactive; blank Active). Codes use letters/numbers/underscores/hyphens and must be unique ignoring case. Manage Customers permission is required.

Project template uses one row per project/company/module. Repeat code and identical common project/AMC fields for all rows of that project. Companies and modules are grouped into one saved project. Use Additional Consultants, separated by semicolons, for multiple people on a module.

Project Code supports up to 50 characters, name 90. Customer must already be active. Choose active project type, Project Manager, Project In-charge, Primary Consultant and module. In-app reference worksheets list current codes, employee IDs and names. General is permitted as a module.

Company blank becomes Company 1. Blank Project Start and Target Finish become today, shown in preview and frozen before commit. Finish must follow start. Industry/contact/budget are optional. Company count is derived from distinct company names, up to 100.

AMC projects require contract start/end, cycle, visits per cycle, hours per visit and attendees. Attendees and additional consultants use semicolon-separated IDs/names/emails. Preferred AMC time defaults 09:00. Non-AMC rows ignore AMC fields with a note.

Preview the file, correct editable cells or choose system master values, revalidate, then Import all rows. Employee-list cells include Add employee from master selectors. Duplicate codes, repeated company/module pairs, missing references and conflicting common fields are listed by source row. Any invalid row blocks the whole transaction.

Project creation requires Create Projects permission and all existing server validation. No tasks, actuals, timesheets, sign-offs or completed go-live records are generated. Customers remain in settings JSON and projects in existing record JSON. No database schema change is needed over v43.

title: 33. Update AMC starting and ending periods
paras: Customer Master and Project Master Excel imports remain available. Import new customers first, then new projects. Existing project codes are add-only; use Update AMC period to edit an existing contract.

On Projects, the AMC contract periods register shows current starting/ending dates and Update AMC period. The AMC project view has the same button. Manage Plans permission is required; unconfigured contracts open full contract setup.

Saved dates load into the form. Enter ordered dates within ten years, add an optional reason, and save. End-only changes preserve the contract ID and existing visit links. The former contract snapshot is appended to history.

A changed start date changes cycle anchors and creates a new contract term ID. Previously tagged visits keep their prior contract links. Existing allocations, actual hours and employee timesheets are retained; no visit data is moved automatically. Coverage changes can alter current compliance counts.

Use Edit AMC contract for attendees, cycles and per-visit hours. The optional Database-AMC-Periods-v45.sql adds a reporting view over existing project JSON, without updating business data or creating new tables. The app does not depend on that view.
